Sizes: built-up areas follow the official catalogue of Roman cities (Hanson 2016). Residents = area × sliding 100–500 people/ha (published method), a density reading, not a census: 12.87 M town residents, 25.7% of the world's people, largest 314,402. Sizes follow the campaign's own ranking: capital, major cities, fortified cities, fortified towns, then unmarked towns (a lore choice). Every resident is taken from surrounding rural cells. 948 of 991 towns (white centre) can be fed when grain may travel (34% of surplus marketed, the share that feeds 95% of Roman city residents at this density reading, Egypt included; see the grain supply map); 43 of the largest stay short.
